transcript.text:
Try these quick checks first:

1. Unplug it before inspecting anything.
2. Check the socket by plugging in something else, and check the Hoover’s plug/fuse if it has one.
3. If it has no power at all, it may have overheated. Leave it unplugged for 30–60 minutes to cool, then try again.
4. Empty the bin / replace the bag and clean or replace filters. A blocked filter can make it cut out or lose suction.
5. Check the hose, wand, floor head and inlet for blockages. A torch and a broom handle can help, but don’t force anything sharp through the hose.
6. If the motor runs but it won’t pick up dirt, check the brush roll underneath for hair, thread, or a jammed belt. Remove tangled hair carefully.
7. For a cordless model, make sure the battery and charger contacts are clean and it has charged fully.

Stop using it if you notice a burning smell, sparking, smoke, a damaged cable, or repeated cutting out — that needs repair rather than further testing.

Is it completely dead, running with no suction, making an unusual noise, or cutting out after a few minutes?
its completely dead. nothing when I switch it on. the socket works, my lamp works in it

If the socket is definitely working and the Hoover is totally dead, the likely causes are the plug fuse, cable/switch fault, thermal cut-out, or internal motor/electronics fault.

Try this safely:

1. Unplug it.
2. Check the cable and plug for cuts, kinks, scorch marks, looseness, or a bent pin. Don’t use it if damaged.
3. If it has a UK-style fused plug: replace the fuse with one of the same rating shown on the plug fuse label (commonly 13 A, sometimes lower). A blown fuse can leave it completely dead.
4. Let it cool down for at least an hour, especially if it stopped during use. Empty the bin/bag and clear filters/blockages before trying again; some models have an overheat cut-out.
5. If it’s cordless, reseat the battery, clean the battery/charger contacts with a dry cloth, and try charging with the battery removed and reinserted.

If a new correct fuse blows again, or it remains dead after cooling, don’t keep trying it: it likely needs a repair (switch, cable connection, thermal fuse, motor, or control board). Avoid opening the main body unless you’re qualified—mains appliances can retain hazardous wiring faults.

If you tell me whether it’s corded or cordless, plus the model number if available, I can narrow down the likely fix.

its a corded one, the red Henry. I haven't got a screwdriver or a spare fuse. there's some old black tape on the cable near the plug, my son did it ages ago. it flickered on once when I moved the wire and then went off

That strongly suggests a broken wire or loose connection in the cable/plug. The fact it briefly worked when the wire was moved is a major warning sign.

Stop using it and unplug it. Do not keep bending or wiggling the lead to make it work. Black tape is not a safe repair for a mains cable; it can mean a shock or fire risk, especially if the copper inside is damaged.

What to do:

• Keep it unplugged and don’t use it until repaired.
• If the taped section is near the plug, a qualified person/electrician or appliance-repair shop can usually fit a new plug and cut back/replace damaged cable.
• On a Henry, the cable may also connect to a rewind reel inside, so if the fault is further along the lead it may need the cable/reel repaired or replaced.
• A repair should normally be straightforward and may be much cheaper than replacing an otherwise working Henry.

Don’t simply add more tape, use an extension lead, or swap the fuse and continue using it — the intermittent behaviour points to the cable itself, not just a fuse.

If there is any exposed copper, melting, burning smell, or warmth around the taped area, keep it away from anything flammable and arrange repair/replacement rather than testing it again.
